task.question: What is the highest recorded temperature in Germany during the 2026 European heatwaves?
task.evidence: 27 June — 2026 European heatwaves: The highest recorded temperature in Germany is taken in Möckern-Drewitz, measuring 41.5 °C (106.7 °F).

answer:
During the heatwaves of June and July 2026, Germany recorded its highest temperature at **41.7 °C (107.1 °F)** in Möckern-Drewitz, Saxony-Anhalt. This record was achieved in late June, marking a significant event during the ongoing European heatwave situation. 

FINAL: 41.7°C (107.1°F) in Möckern-Drewitz, Germany

Starting in late May 2026, several severe heatwaves affected Europe. Temperature records were broken in Austria, Belarus, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, France, Germany, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. The first heatwave began on 24 May, with temperatures higher than normal and several heat-related deaths.
A second, more severe heatwave began on 17 June, just days before the summer solstice. In France, Météo-France declared 23 June the country's hottest day since measurements began in 1947, with temperatures reaching 44.3 °C (111.7 °F) in Pissos, 42.1 °C (107.8 °F) in Bordeaux, and a June record of 40.9 °C (105.6 °F) in Paris. In May, new temperature records were set at 46 GeoSphere Austria stations. Of those, Lienz had the highest temperature, recording 33.3 °C (91.9 °F) on 26 May. The city also had a record eight hot days in May, each with a temperature of at least 30 °C (86 °F), beating the previous record of three set in 2001.
